text:
security-bot: [ALERT] git-leak-scan: potential credential found in history for repo infra/terraform-modules/network (scanner:v2.1)
security-bot: snippet: 'aws_access_key_id = \"AKIAxxxxxxxxxxxx\"' (match confidence: 0.82)
Maria Chen: WTF, which commit? can someone pull the offending commit hash?
Samir Patel: I ran the scan locally, looks like commit 7f3a2b4 touched module aws/providers.tf on 2022-11-03
Rajesh Kumar: Noted. Is that from a CI artifact or committed to Git history? we need to know scope (branch/main/merge)
DevOps Runner: artifact check: found matching blob in gitlab-runner cache archive for job infra:plan:2022-11-04 (artifact id 38291)
Elaine Park: Ok containment plan: 1) revoke the key 2) rotate any linked IAM role 3) remove blobs from history 4) notify affected customers if any. Agree?
Troy Simmons: +1. Who has permission to revoke the key?
Samir Patel: I can revoke it. Confirming key id: AKIAxxxxxxxxxxxx -> policy shows long-lived user 'terraform-deploy'
Maria Chen: Stop all runners that can access that repo's artifacts until we confirm no other leaks.
DevOps Runner: Runner stopped: gitlab-shared-03. Retention for artifacts increased to 30d for audit, but we just paused writes.
Rajesh Kumar: Samir, rotate and revoke steps please. Also file a JIRA incident and mark P2 for now.
Samir Patel: Done revoke: IAM console shows key inactive, deleted access keys for user terraform-deploy. JIRA IN-7642 created.
Maria Chen: For history rewrite: we'll run git filter-repo to purge blob and force-push. Rajesh: can you coordinate with legal on disclosure window in case of customer impact?
Rajesh Kumar: Looping in legal via DM. No customer tokens referenced so far, seems infra account only. Legal says hold on public comms until we finish scope.
Elaine Park: Run BFG or filter-repo? prefer git-filter-repo and then rotate downstream tokens.
Samir Patel: Using git-filter-repo. Commands:

```
git filter-repo --invert-paths --paths-glob '*/providers.tf'
# then rewrite refs and force push to origin and update protected branch policies
```

We'll mark the specific blob SHA for removal first.
Troy Simmons: Note: we need to preserve CI pipelines. After force-push we'll add a migration script to re-create missing refs for active pipelines to avoid broken runs.
Maria Chen: Also add post-incident controls: 1) tighten RBAC for service users 2) enforce git-secrets pre-commit on terraform modules 3) turn on object-level audit logging for runner cache 4) integrate KMS to encrypt artifact-store with customer-managed key
DevOps Runner: Audit logs: enabled S3 access logging + CloudTrail for artifact bucket; KMS CMK rotated and key policy restricted to ops-role only (pending approval)
Rajesh Kumar: Quick vuln triage: check other repos/modules for same pattern. I'll run a global grep across org and a targeted git-history scan for similar aws_access_key_id patterns.
Samir Patel: I pushed a small MR that adds a pre-commit hook and CI check: fail pipeline if git-secrets find matches. MR: infra/ci#1203
Maria Chen: Good. Postmortem owners: Samir (revocation+cleanup), Rajesh (scope & legal), Elaine (post-incident controls), Troy (runner migration). Target postmortem doc due in 5 business days.
Troy Simmons: Also propose adding ephemeral KMS-wrapped deploy keys for terraform; PR incoming.
Rajesh Kumar: After history rewrite, we'll need a communications plan for internal teams: infra, support, security, and exec. Keep comms internal until legal OKs external.
Samir Patel: Final note: running full org scan now, ETA ~2h. Will update thread when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maria Chen: Thanks all. Keep thread for updates. Marking channel pinned message to IN-7642.
Samir Patel: scan complete: no other matches beyond network module and one leftover artifact in runner cache (now deleted). Closing initial containment. Next: postmortem + controls.
Elaine Park: Scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 10:00am. Agenda: root cause, why creds were committed, CI artifact retention policy, RBAC & KMS follow-ups, timeline of actions. Invite: infra, security, legal, devex.
Rajesh Kumar: Adding retrospective action items to IN-7642: enforce short-lived keys for terraform users, integrate secrets-rotator, daily leak-scan cron.
Maria Chen: closing notes: good response time. We'll keep the runbook updated. :thumbsup:
